skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Guides Docker containerization with multi-stage builds, Compose orchestration, image optimization, diagnostics, and production practices.
skill.summary: Build, optimize, troubleshoot, and harden Docker applications with reusable workflows and examples.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation syntax, local health checks, or protective ignore rules. Confirmed risks include predictable secrets, external diagnostics, credential disclosure, destructive cleanup, exposed Elasticsearch, and mutable images.

remediation.suggestion: Require externally supplied secrets or Docker secrets, remove public defaults, and document credential rotation before deployment.

remediation.issue: Unauthenticated services published on host ports
remediation.suggestion: Enable Elasticsearch security and bind development administration services to loopback or isolated internal networks.

remediation.issue: Complete environment output can reveal secrets
remediation.suggestion: Remove the env command or require confirmation and redact variables matching password, token, key, and secret names.

remediation.issue: Forced Docker cleanup can delete persistent data
remediation.suggestion: Show affected resources, require explicit confirmation, and separate volume pruning behind a dedicated destructive option.
Pin every image to a reviewed version or digest and update it through a controlled dependency process.

remediation.issue: External connectivity test uses a fixed public address
remediation.suggestion: Make external diagnostics opt-in and allow users to configure an approved health endpoint.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Default Service Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The example assigns predictable passwords to database, cache, queue, monitoring, and administration services while publishing several host ports.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited line assigns a literal, predictable password in a runnable Compose example.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Elasticsearch Exposure
semantic_findings.description: Elasticsearch security is disabled while port 9200 is published, allowing unauthenticated access when the host is reachable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The configuration explicitly disables xpack security and maps Elasticsearch to a host port.

semantic_findings.title: Container Secret Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The env command prints every container environment variable, which commonly includes credentials and tokens, into terminal or agent output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly executes env inside the selected container and prints its complete output.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup command forces removal of stopped containers, unused images, volumes, and networks without a confirmation or preview.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Every prune command uses -f, and volume pruning can permanently remove application data.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Production Image Tags
semantic_findings.description: Several runnable services use latest tags, so future pulls can retrieve unreviewed image changes or compromised upstream releases.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited image references explicitly use the mutable latest tag.

content.value_statement: Containerizing applications consistently requires many connected Docker decisions. This skill guides builds, Compose services, diagnostics, optimization, and production hardening with reusable examples.
actual_capabilities: Creates multi-stage Dockerfile plans for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust applications.
Designs Docker Compose services with dependencies, networks, volumes, health checks, and environment-specific overrides.
Explains layer caching, BuildKit cache mounts, minimal images, and non-root runtime users.
Provides Docker commands for building, running, inspecting, logging, restarting, and troubleshooting containers.
Includes a Bash helper for health checks, backups, cleanup, network inspection, and image analysis.
Reviews container configurations for production readiness, resource limits, monitoring, and deployment practices.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to the application, directory structure, ports, and package manager.
The helper script requires local Docker access and can perform destructive cleanup operations.
The included Compose example contains development credentials and must not be deployed unchanged.
The skill does not replace vulnerability scanning, secret management, or an orchestration platform.

use_cases.title: Containerize a New Service
use_cases.description: Create a compact, non-root multi-stage image with dependency caching and a practical health check.

use_cases.title: Standardize Local Environments
use_cases.description: Define repeatable application, database, cache, and worker services with Compose networks and volumes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Production Deployment
use_cases.description: Review images and Compose settings for security, observability, resource limits, and controlled updates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile for [application] using [runtime]. Use a non-root user, add a health check, and explain each stage.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a Local Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Docker Compose setup for [services]. Include isolated networks, named volumes, health checks, and development overrides.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [symptom] for container [name]. Provide ordered inspection steps, expected evidence, and reversible fixes before destructive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Docker files for secrets, privileges, network exposure, mutable images, resource limits, and recovery risks. Prioritize fixes by impact.

output_examples.input: Containerize a Node.js API for production.
output_examples.output: A two-stage image plan separates dependency installation from runtime, uses a non-root account, and adds a localhost health check.

output_examples.input: Why does my Compose service start before PostgreSQL is ready?
output: Keep application retry logic for temporary database failures.

output_examples.output: The review identifies build-only packages, cache retention, layer ordering, and a slim runtime stage as the main reduction opportunities.

best_practices: Pin reviewed image versions or digests and update them through a controlled process.
Keep secrets outside images and Compose files by using a dedicated secret manager.
Preview cleanup and deployment effects, then require confirmation before data-changing commands.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy example passwords, fallback secrets, or exposed administration services.
Do not use mutable latest tags for production images.
Do not run broad prune commands before reviewing containers, images, networks, and volumes.

faq.question: Does this skill install Docker?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but Docker and Compose must be installed with appropriate host permissions.

faq.question: Which application runtimes are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust, with patterns adaptable to other runtimes.

faq.question: Can I use the Compose example in production?
faq.answer: Not unchanged. Replace credentials, restrict ports, enable service security, pin images, and review resource requirements.

faq.question: Does the helper script modify Docker resources?
faq.answer: Yes. Restart, backup, and cleanup commands change resources, and cleanup can permanently remove unused volumes.

faq.question: Does the skill create Kubernetes manifests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Dockerfiles and Docker Compose, though its image practices can support later orchestration.

faq.question: How should secrets be supplied?
faq.answer: Use Docker secrets or an external secret manager, avoid fallback values, and keep secret files outside build contexts.
